story_title: Natural Disasters and Epidemics: A Century of Human Impact
story_subtitle: Analyzing the deadliest events, their temporal trends, and comparative mortality across disaster types from 1900 to 2017

story_pieces.narration: The 1976 Nicaragua earthquake, with 276,994 deaths, stands as the single deadliest natural disaster in the dataset, surpassing all other individual events.
story_pieces.question: Which specific natural disaster event caused the highest number of deaths in the dataset?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart (events vs. deaths) with top 5 highlighted

story_pieces.narration: Total deaths from all natural disasters peaked in 1917 (2.5 million) and 1907 (1.3 million), declining to around 200,000 by 2017, showing a long-term downward trend.
story_pieces.question: How has the total mortality from all natural disasters changed over the 20th and 21st centuries?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (years vs. cumulative deaths) with trendline

story_pieces.narration: Epidemics accounted for 82% of total deaths from all natural disasters (1900-2017), with the 1918 Spanish flu pandemic alone causing 449,700 deaths, dwarfing other disaster types.
story_pieces.question: How do epidemics compare to other natural disaster types in terms of mortality contribution?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (disaster types vs. deaths) with epidemic highlighted

story_pieces.narration: The 1931 China flood (3.7 million deaths) and 1928 global drought (3 million deaths) represent the most extreme mortality events in the dataset, far exceeding even the deadliest earthquakes.
story_pieces.question: Which disaster type and year produced the highest death tolls in the dataset?
story_pieces.visualization: scatter plot (disaster type vs. deaths) with year annotations

story_pieces.narration: While epidemic mortality declined sharply after 1945, extreme weather events like the 2010 Russian heatwave (55,000 deaths) and 2015-2016 global extreme temperatures (74,250 deaths) show modern climate-related risks.
story_pieces.question: How have mortality patterns shifted between epidemics and extreme weather in recent decades?
story_pieces.visualization: grouped bar chart (decades vs. epidemic deaths/extreme weather deaths)
